title: Scaffold sync
lede: How shared rules and skills flow from the scaffold repo into project repos, and how a project's generic fix flows back up.

bootstrap.name: Bootstrap
bootstrap.role: The first time, install the sync script, then run it once the user confirms.
details: If bin/sync-from-scaffold.sh is missing, a curl of bootstrap.sh installs the script only.

down.name: Sync down
down.role: /sync-scaffold merges scaffold's files into the project on the current branch.
details: The manifest, scaffold-files.txt, lists the files scaffold ships.
A file that differs, has a base and has no uncommitted edits gets a 3-way merge from the last synced commit.

details.t: When a merge can't be automatic
more: No base and the file differs: the incoming copy is saved as a .scaffold-new sidecar to review.
Conflict markers: resolve, commit, re-run with --mark-resolved.

risks: A sidecar is not applied: the original file is unchanged until someone diffs and merges it.

upstream.name: Upstream
upstream.role: /upstream splits a project change into its universal half and moves that half into scaffold.
details: Work in a scaffold worktree off origin/main, never its main checkout.
Make the change the scaffold way; a new skill needs its wrappers, RESOLVER entry, manifest line and test.
npm test and eslint (0 errors) must pass, plus typecheck when TypeScript changed.

pr.name: Scaffold PR
pr.role: Open a scaffold PR that says why the change is universal, and merge it only if authorized.
details: The PR names the consumer that needed it.
Read the real check conclusions; a skipped check is not a pass.
Remove the worktree after the merge.

back.name: Sync back
back.role: Run /sync-scaffold again on a project branch to pull the merged change back in.
details: Keep .scaffold-keep paths and merge diverged files.
Put the project-specific half in the project's own policy file.
Then the project's own gates, PR and authorized merge.

more: Exports chosen skills into another repo in a target harness's format.
.sync/hoisted records the name, harness and pinned ref; --from-manifest replays it.

qs: What decides whether a change belongs in scaffold or stays in the project?

consumer.d: A project repo that syncs from scaffold.

manifest.d: The list of files scaffold ships to consumers.

sidecar.d: A .scaffold-new copy of scaffold's version saved beside your file for review; writing it leaves your file unchanged.

keep.d: The consumer's list of paths the sync never touches.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold's shared agent rules and skills sync into project repos and how fixes flow back.
